description: An AI assistant for photographers on Mac. Lazur sees your screen, answers out loud, drafts client replies and guides you through Lightroom and Gmail.
intro: An AI assistant for photographers on Mac helps with the work around the shoot: client email, invoices, file hunts and menu searches. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that sees your screen while you hold ⌥⌘, points at what you ask about and answers out loud. This page shows where that help fits, where it does not, and what a working day looks like.
tldr: Editing took the biggest share of business time in one 2020 survey of wedding photographers, at 55%.
Admin, email and communication filled much of the rest. You may also be your own billing and records team.
Lazur points at controls, explains menus, answers out loud and drafts text. It does not click, send or edit files for you.

blocks.text: Where a photographer's working time goes

The clearest number comes from a 2020 survey of more than 300 UK wedding photographers. Your Perfect Wedding Photographer ran it, and Fstoppers reported the results. It put editing at 55% of business time. Business and admin took 18%. Culling took 11%. Communication, such as emails to set up jobs, took 7%. Shooting came in at as little as 4%.

Read those numbers with care. The sample was small, covered one country, and came from a company that sells to photographers. It also predates the current wave of AI editing and culling tools. The listed shares add up to 95%, so treat the picture as rough. Still, the direction is clear. Most business time goes to making pictures usable and to the paperwork around them.

Self-employment adds to the load. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics says 67% of photographers are self-employed. Its handbook lists marketing to attract clients, keeping records, charging customers and paying bills as normal duties. If you work alone, nobody else handles those tasks. You handle them between shoots, or late on a Sunday.
Email is the part that never closes

Email has its own numbers, but they come from general office work. Microsoft's June 2025 study says the average employee gets 117 emails a day. The same release says 40% of employees check email before 6 a.m. A 2012 McKinsey figure, read through UPeak, puts email at 28% of the workweek for interaction workers. No study of photographers' inboxes turned up. Treat these as a warning, not a measurement of your week.
Most photographer email falls into a few kinds of mail. Each kind has a predictable answer, which makes it a good first job for an assistant:

items: Booking inquiries that ask for a date, a price and a yes or no.
Gallery delivery questions, expired links and password resets.
Reschedules that start with one line and end with new dates.
Review requests, referrals and thank-you notes after a job.

blocks.text: Your inbox still needs you. Lazur does not send mail for you. It helps you read, answer and check the details before you press send.
Using Lazur for client replies in Gmail

Start with the reply, not the inbox. Hold fn and say the answer. Lazur dictates clean, formatted text at your cursor in any app, including the Gmail compose window. Dictation is included with Lazur, so you can use it all day. Snippets help with the parts you repeat, such as your delivery policy or your session fee rules. To test your own speaking pace, try the [speaking versus typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test).

When you need to find something, hold ⌥⌘ and ask. Ask where the Calendar icon is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. You click it yourself. Lazur does not click buttons, so it will not send the email or change a setting for you. That rule matters most when a client reply sets a date.
Here is one moment from a client thread. A couple asks to move a Saturday session to Sunday. You need to see if the slot is free before you answer.

For the setup around Gmail, use the browser steps. Build your signature once with [the signature steps](/how-to/create-an-email-signature-in-gmail). Set up a [filter for client mail](/how-to/create-a-filter-in-gmail) so inquiries land in one label. Then use Lazur for the words, not the settings.
Culling and editing with an AI assistant

Culling and editing take the most time, and they are the parts you should decide yourself. Lightroom Classic 15.0 came out on October 28, 2025. It needs macOS 14 Sonoma or later, and it supports macOS 26 Tahoe. Check Adobe's requirements page before you update, because we could not confirm the current list from Adobe's own site.

Lazur fits the search part of editing. Ask, "Where do I set the export size?" and Lazur circles the control. Ask what clarity does to skin, and it explains in plain words. It can guide you through an export preset one click at a time. It does not pick keepers, set exposure or retouch a face. Those calls stay with you.

The same rule covers other apps. For retouching order and shortcuts, read the [Photoshop workflow guide](/for/photographers/photoshop). For watermarks, exports and portfolio pages, read the [Canva guide](/for/photographers/canva). Lazur can point at and explain controls in both apps. You make the edits.

blocks.title: Keep the second look
blocks.text: A faster menu does not replace a second look at the frame. Use Lazur to find the control, then make the pick yourself. Check sharpness at full size before you reject a frame.

This is one plausible day for a wedding and portrait photographer. The times are examples. Each line shows something you could say out loud, and the result shows what Lazur does with it. Notice how often the answer is a pointer, a draft or a guided step. Lazur does not do the work in the app for you.
Setup, privacy and client data

Lazur is a Mac app for macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Hold fn to dictate. Lazur keeps memory of what you asked and did, and that memory stays on your Mac.

Privacy works like this. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer you. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

blocks.title: Client data comes first
blocks.text: Client addresses, payment details, unreleased work and any health or legal notes need care. Follow your contracts and local data rules before you share anything with an AI tool. This page makes no compliance claims for your work.

Practical habits help. Share the minimum. Ask about one sentence, not the whole client file. Hide names and card numbers before you ask for help with a screenshot, because the screenshot goes to AI providers to answer. If a client contract bans outside tools, follow the contract.
Common mistakes with an AI assistant for photographers

items: Expecting Lazur to click. It points, explains and guides, then waits for you.
Sending a drafted reply without reading the price, date and deposit.
Pasting a whole client file when one question would do.
Asking for a Lightroom fix without checking your macOS version first.
Judging the tool from one afternoon. Run it on a real inbox for a week.

blocks.text: Start small. Pick one repeat task, such as booking replies, and run it for a week. Note how long it takes before and after. Then decide whether the next task is worth it. When you are ready, [download Lazur](/download) or read [the pricing page](/pricing) for current plans and trial terms.

faq.question: Is there an AI assistant for photographers that works in any Mac app?
faq.answer: Yes, Lazur works across Mac apps. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about what is on screen, and it answers out loud. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. It points, explains and guides. It does not run the app for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my photos in Lightroom or Photoshop?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not edit files or operate other apps. It can point at a slider, explain what it does, and guide you through an export one click at a time. You make the edits and the decisions.

faq.question: Which macOS version do I need for Lightroom Classic?
faq.answer: Lightroom Classic 15.0 came out on October 28, 2025. It needs macOS 14 Sonoma or later and supports macOS 26 Tahoe. Lightroom Queen reported this. We could not confirm it on Adobe's own pages, so check there before you update.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: Will my client photos or emails train AI models?
faq.answer: Lazur says content is never used to train AI models. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Still, read your client contracts before you share client details with any tool.

faq.question: Do I have to hold the key the whole time?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask a question. Hold fn to dictate text at your cursor.

faq.question: Can an AI assistant take over my admin time on its own?
faq.answer: Not really. It can read the screen, draft text and guide you through a task. The survey numbers show admin is a large share of time. They do not show how much an assistant saves. No photographer-specific study covers that yet.

painPoints.title: Editing takes most of the week
painPoints.text: In one 2020 survey of wedding photographers, editing took 55% of business time. Culling took another 11%, so photo work takes most of your business time.

painPoints.title: Admin has no fixed slot
painPoints.text: Business and admin took 18% in that survey, and communication took 7%. These tasks are small and frequent, so they fill every gap in the day.

painPoints.title: You are the back office
painPoints.text: The BLS says 67% of photographers are self-employed. Billing, records and marketing fall to you, and nobody else reminds you to do them.

painPoints.title: Email arrives all day
painPoints.text: Microsoft's 2025 study found the average employee gets 117 emails a day. No study tracks photographers' inboxes, so expect your own count to vary.

painPoints.title: Menus hide the fix
painPoints.text: Lightroom Classic 15.0 came out in October 2025. Finding one control in a dense app is a search problem, not a skill problem.
